# DrawPacket — Cycle Study design research

**Direction:** Treat the monthly construction draw as an editorial cycle, not a fintech dashboard. Keep chalk `#F5F5F1`, oxblood `#642A37`, ink `#252225`, and lilac `#DFDBE8`; use the **Cadence** mark—two staggered, diagonally split vertical capsules—as a recurring *static* registration device. The audience is the GC project accountant. This is a research direction, not a claim about a built product or its payment or compliance capabilities.

## 1. Ten button and card hover patterns

These are **proposed interactions, not animations observed on reference sites**. Use a finite vocabulary: a short reveal, a line movement, or a small icon exchange—not all three on one component. Make every action available without hover; retain a visible keyboard-focus indicator. Apply hover-only effects where hovering is available, and suppress nonessential movement when reduced motion is requested. [web:115][web:122][web:45]

| Pattern | DrawPacket use | Interaction and static equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Directional wipe | Primary “Explore the cycle” button | Oxblood fill crosses behind a stationary label; on focus or reduced motion, switch fill without travel. |
| 2. Editorial underline | Text links and section-index links | A fine rule extends from the left; show the full rule on focus and touch activation. |
| 3. Arrow exchange | Buttons linking to the next step | Outgoing arrow yields to an incoming arrow in the same bounded slot; show one static arrow without motion. |
| 4. Border trace | Featured case or process card | One short corner rule extends along an edge; use a complete, high-contrast border for focus. |
| 5. Icon morph | Expandable process details | A small plus changes to minus **only when expanded**; use text or `aria-expanded` to convey state, not shape alone. |
| 6. Source reveal | Research-backed insight card | A persistent “Source” label opens a citation/detail panel; never hide the citation exclusively behind hover. |
| 7. Caption lift | Industrial photograph card | Caption moves a few pixels into its reserved space; leave caption visible in the default and touch states. |
| 8. Index emphasis | Timeline-step card | Mono step number changes weight or color while the card stays still; retain a distinct focus outline. |
| 9. Diagram highlight | Draw-package component card | One corresponding line or part changes to oxblood; keep the component name visible without the highlight. |
| 10. Surface tint | Secondary card or link block | Chalk shifts subtly toward lilac; pair the tint with a border or underline so state is not color-only. |

Prefer CSS for these bounded states. MDN advises animating `transform` and `opacity` where practical rather than properties that trigger layout or repaint; test any line or border treatment rather than assuming it is free. [web:111]

## 2. Open-font shortlist

**Recommended working stack:** Roboto Serif at a deliberately narrow width for headlines; Bodoni Moda for a short, sturdy wordmark trial; DM Sans for UI; IBM Plex Mono for dates, step numbers, and *verified* figures. Roboto Serif is the strongest literal match for “condensed”: its source describes widths from condensed to extended. Bodoni Moda offers optical sizes but should **not** be described as a condensed family; Instrument Serif is an expressive alternative, likewise not a condensed solution. [web:179][web:22][web:145]

| Role | Font and official source URL | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Narrow editorial headlines | [Roboto Serif](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto+Serif) | First test: narrow `wdth` setting, generous size, restrained line lengths; verify the actual downloaded variable file and widths. [web:178][web:172] |
| More dramatic headline alternative | [Bodoni Moda](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Bodoni+Moda) | Test for major, brief headlines—not dense UI or a claimed condensed cut. [web:22] |
| Softer editorial alternative | [Newsreader](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Newsreader) | Trial for longer editorial headings or explanatory copy. [web:20] |
| Expressive display accent | [Instrument Serif](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Instrument+Serif) | Use sparingly if its character wins the visual tests; it does not resolve the condensed requirement. [web:145] |
| Neutral UI | [DM Sans](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/DM+Sans) | Navigation, forms, captions, and longer interface text. [web:118] |
| Numbers and metadata | [IBM Plex Mono](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/IBM+Plex+Mono) | Month labels, drawing references, and clearly sourced numerical data. [web:119] |

Download selected families from their **Google Fonts specimen pages**, keep each bundled license with the files, and self-host only the weights, axes, and character sets needed. Google says its catalog is open source and permits commercial use, but the **license shipped with each family** governs redistribution; its self-hosting guide covers local font files. [web:16][web:169][web:171]

## 3. Motion and content system

| Element | Proposed treatment | Guardrail and source |
|---|---|---|
| Cycle timeline | Show all step names in the document first; on entry, reveal one connecting rule and lightly emphasize the current step. | Use `IntersectionObserver` for one-time entry or CSS view timelines as an enhancement. Scroll-driven timelines are not universally supported, so the static timeline must remain complete. [web:103][web:47][web:46] |
| Jurisdiction map | Use a restrained, labeled map or region list to explain that requirements **vary by jurisdiction**; select a place to read its *sourced* context. | Do **not** animate dots into a purported service footprint, demand heatmap, or coverage claim. |
| Tier network | Present tiers as a legible hierarchy of roles and handoffs; highlight one relationship on selection. | Avoid a growing network animation that implies an actual partner count or reach. |
| Draw process | Use a numbered, left-to-right sequence—assemble, review, resolve, submit—as an **illustrative concept**, not a representation of current product behavior. | Keep text and diagram understandable before animation; use GSAP only if sequencing materially helps. `gsap.matchMedia()` can select and clean up reduced-motion and responsive treatments. [web:31][web:34] |
| Counters | Prefer static, attributed figures. If a verified count merits emphasis, reveal its final value once. | Never invent ROI, time saved, transaction volume, payment speed, or compliance rates. |
| Short explainer video | Storyboard: **1** dated jobsite detail; **2** paper-to-document organization; **3** a clearly labeled monthly review sequence; **4** quiet Cadence-mark end frame and invitation to learn more. | Make it user-played with a poster, controls, captions, and descriptive transcript or description as appropriate; avoid a looping hero. A poster with `preload="none"` is a documented lightweight option. [web:188][web:183][web:184] |

**Reusable motion vocabulary:** *register* (a fine line appears), *advance* (one step gains emphasis), and *resolve* (a detail changes to its selected state). Keep travel small, avoid perpetual movement, and offer static states. W3C documents reduced-motion treatment for interaction-triggered animation; automatically moving content that runs beyond five seconds alongside other content needs a pause, stop, or hide mechanism under WCAG’s stated conditions. [web:45][web:49]

## 4. Third-party marks: official sources and limits

| Brand | Official guideline / asset URL | Design decision |
|---|---|---|
| LinkedIn | [Brand downloads](https://brand.linkedin.com/downloads); [**[in]** icon rules](https://brand.linkedin.com/in-logo); [full LinkedIn Logo rules](https://brand.linkedin.com/linkedin-logo) | An approved **[in]** icon can serve as a link to the relevant LinkedIn page under its stated rules; do not recolor or combine it with Cadence. The **full LinkedIn Logo** requires an existing relationship and Brand or Trademark License. LinkedIn specifies transparent PNG for that full-logo download and says other formats may be supplied on request—**do not promise an official SVG download**. [web:2][web:4][web:3] |
| Crunchbase | [Official press assets](https://about.crunchbase.com/press); [terms of service](https://about.crunchbase.com/terms-of-service) | The press page lists standard and white logos, but the available official page evidence does **not** establish a downloadable vector format or a separate public brand-guideline page. Source any proposed use from that press page and request the current vector and usage permission through its listed PR contact rather than treating third-party SVG libraries as approved assets. [web:1][web:77] |

## 5. Page-level industrial art direction

These are **palette and texture proposals**, not documented DrawPacket assets or evidence of geographic reach.

| Page | Palette emphasis | Realistic visual texture |
|---|---|---|
| Home | Chalk field, ink type, one oxblood action | Cropped plan-sheet folds, graphite registration marks, and a single photographed construction material detail. |
| How it works | Chalk and ink; lilac for secondary annotations | Ruled document margins, stamped dates, and carefully spaced drawing-reference labels. |
| Who it’s for | Warm chalk with oxblood section markers | Desk-level paper, marked-up schedules, and hands reviewing documents—specific to accounting work, not generic hard-hat stock. |
| Jurisdictions / network | Ink-led map with lilac boundaries | Survey-style linework and labeled regions; no glowing pins, heatmaps, or implied operating footprint. |
| About / contact | Quiet chalk and ink; oxblood sparingly | Material close-ups—concrete formwork, steel, or vellum—used as crops with enough clear space for readable text. |

Use the Cadence capsules as a repeatable diagram marker, not a bouncing mascot. Before selecting any photograph, caption, statistic, jurisdiction, or process assertion for publication, verify that it depicts—or is plainly labeled as illustrative of—what the copy says.

Prefer CSS for these bounded states. MDN advises animating `transform` and `opacity` where practical rather than properties that trigger layout or repaint; test any line or border treatment rather than assuming it is free. [web:111]

## 2. Open-font shortlist

**Recommended working stack:** Roboto Serif at a deliberately narrow width for headlines; Bodoni Moda for a short, sturdy wordmark trial; DM Sans for UI; IBM Plex Mono for dates, step numbers, and *verified* figures. Roboto Serif is the strongest literal match for “condensed”: its source describes widths from condensed to extended. Bodoni Moda offers optical sizes but should **not** be described as a condensed family; Instrument Serif is an expressive alternative, likewise not a condensed solution. [web:179][web:22][web:145]

| Role | Font and official source URL | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Narrow editorial headlines | [Roboto Serif](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto+Serif) | First test: narrow `wdth` setting, generous size, restrained line lengths; verify the actual downloaded variable file and widths. [web:178][web:172] |
| More dramatic headline alternative | [Bodoni Moda](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Bodoni+Moda) | Test for major, brief headlines—not dense UI or a claimed condensed cut. [web:22] |
| Softer editorial alternative | [Newsreader](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Newsreader) | Trial for longer editorial headings or explanatory copy. [web:20] |
| Expressive display accent | [Instrument Serif](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Instrument+Serif) | Use sparingly if its character wins the visual tests; it does not resolve the condensed requirement. [web:145] |
| Neutral UI | [DM Sans](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/DM+Sans) | Navigation, forms, captions, and longer interface text. [web:118] |
| Numbers and metadata | [IBM Plex Mono](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/IBM+Plex+Mono) | Month labels, drawing references, and clearly sourced numerical data. [web:119] |

Download selected families from their **Google Fonts specimen pages**, keep each bundled license with the files, and self-host only the weights, axes, and character sets needed. Google says its catalog is open source and permits commercial use, but the **license shipped with each family** governs redistribution; its self-hosting guide covers local font files. [web:16][web:169][web:171]

## 3. Motion and content system

| Element | Proposed treatment | Guardrail and source |
|---|---|---|
| Cycle timeline | Show all step names in the document first; on entry, reveal one connecting rule and lightly emphasize the current step. | Use `IntersectionObserver` for one-time entry or CSS view timelines as an enhancement. Scroll-driven timelines are not universally supported, so the static timeline must remain complete. [web:103][web:47][web:46] |
| Jurisdiction map | Use a restrained, labeled map or region list to explain that requirements **vary by jurisdiction**; select a place to read its *sourced* context. | Do **not** animate dots into a purported service footprint, demand heatmap, or coverage claim. |
| Tier network | Present tiers as a legible hierarchy of roles and handoffs; highlight one relationship on selection. | Avoid a growing network animation that implies an actual partner count or reach. |
| Draw process | Use a numbered, left-to-right sequence—assemble, review, resolve, submit—as an **illustrative concept**, not a representation of current product behavior. | Keep text and diagram understandable before animation; use GSAP only if sequencing materially helps. `gsap.matchMedia()` can select and clean up reduced-motion and responsive treatments. [web:31][web:34] |
| Counters | Prefer static, attributed figures. If a verified count merits emphasis, reveal its final value once. | Never invent ROI, time saved, transaction volume, payment speed, or compliance rates. |
| Short explainer video | Storyboard: **1** dated jobsite detail; **2** paper-to-document organization; **3** a clearly labeled monthly review sequence; **4** quiet Cadence-mark end frame and invitation to learn more. | Make it user-played with a poster, controls, captions, and descriptive transcript or description as appropriate; avoid a looping hero. A poster with `preload="none"` is a documented lightweight option. [web:188][web:183][web:184] |

**Reusable motion vocabulary:** *register* (a fine line appears), *advance* (one step gains emphasis), and *resolve* (a detail changes to its selected state). Keep travel small, avoid perpetual movement, and offer static states. W3C documents reduced-motion treatment for interaction-triggered animation; automatically moving content that runs beyond five seconds alongside other content needs a pause, stop, or hide mechanism under WCAG’s stated conditions. [web:45][web:49]

## 4. Third-party marks: official sources and limits

| Brand | Official guideline / asset URL | Design decision |
|---|---|---|
| LinkedIn | [Brand downloads](https://brand.linkedin.com/downloads); [**[in]** icon rules](https://brand.linkedin.com/in-logo); [full LinkedIn Logo rules](https://brand.linkedin.com/linkedin-logo) | An approved **[in]** icon can serve as a link to the relevant LinkedIn page under its stated rules; do not recolor or combine it with Cadence. The **full LinkedIn Logo** requires an existing relationship and Brand or Trademark License. LinkedIn specifies transparent PNG for that full-logo download and says other formats may be supplied on request—**do not promise an official SVG download**. [web:2][web:4][web:3] |
| Crunchbase | [Official press assets](https://about.crunchbase.com/press); [terms of service](https://about.crunchbase.com/terms-of-service) | The press page lists standard and white logos, but the available official page evidence does **not** establish a downloadable vector format or a separate public brand-guideline page. Source any proposed use from that press page and request the current vector and usage permission through its listed PR contact rather than treating third-party SVG libraries as approved assets. [web:1][web:77] |

## 5. Page-level industrial art direction

These are **palette and texture proposals**, not documented DrawPacket assets or evidence of geographic reach.

| Page | Palette emphasis | Realistic visual texture |
|---|---|---|
| Home | Chalk field, ink type, one oxblood action | Cropped plan-sheet folds, graphite registration marks, and a single photographed construction material detail. |
| How it works | Chalk and ink; lilac for secondary annotations | Ruled document margins, stamped dates, and carefully spaced drawing-reference labels. |
| Who it’s for | Warm chalk with oxblood section markers | Desk-level paper, marked-up schedules, and hands reviewing documents—specific to accounting work, not generic hard-hat stock. |
| Jurisdictions / network | Ink-led map with lilac boundaries | Survey-style linework and labeled regions; no glowing pins, heatmaps, or implied operating footprint. |
| About / contact | Quiet chalk and ink; oxblood sparingly | Material close-ups—concrete formwork, steel, or vellum—used as crops with enough clear space for readable text. |

Use the Cadence capsules as a repeatable diagram marker, not a bouncing mascot. Before selecting any photograph, caption, statistic, jurisdiction, or process assertion for publication, verify that it depicts—or is plainly labeled as illustrative of—what the copy says.
